nodes.label: Quarterly Architecture Review (2026-08-24)
nodes.author: d.okafor
nodes.rationale: Reviewed the single-process, single-artifact architecture against two quarters of incidents; none of the four postmortems was caused by the single-process model itself, so the architecture was reaffirmed. Adopted a standing design-review question distinguishing build/typecheck-catchable regressions from convention-dependent correctness.

nodes.label: Webhook Delivery Backlog Incident
nodes.author: k.ferreira
nodes.rationale: A customer's scripted bulk-import fanned out roughly 27,000 pending webhook delivery rows almost instantly; CLAIM_BATCH=25 per minute-long tick was never load-tested against a realistic burst, and the cross-tenant, oldest-first claim order meant every organization's deliveries were delayed, not just the triggering customer's. Raising CLAIM_BATCH alone was judged insufficient; a per-organization fairness mechanism was tracked as a separate, still-open action item.

nodes.label: Board and Settings Server Component Crash Incident
nodes.author: m.lindqvist
nodes.norm_label: board and settings server component crash incident
nodes.rationale: A refactor's file-move tooling preserved import statements but dropped the leading "use client" directive from two Client Components, which is not a build-time or type error in Next.js 16 and only surfaces as a hard render error when a DOM onClick handler is serialized from server-rendered output. pnpm build and pnpm typecheck both passed on the broken commit; the fix was an ESLint rule plus a render smoke test to make the risk mechanically detectable rather than only documented.

nodes.label: Cross-Tenant Issue List Leak Incident
nodes.author: m.lindqvist
nodes.rationale: A temporary diagnostic script bypassed listIssues and queried the table directly, omitting the orgId predicate that is the tenant boundary in this codebase. Because there is no database-level row-security layer, the boundary lives entirely in disciplined, reviewed code, and a hand-written query that skips the sanctioned helper is unprotected by construction. assertOrgScope() could not have caught it because the script never reached the service layer where a resolved Actor exists.

nodes.label: Digest Storm Incident
nodes.author: t.abara
nodes.rationale: A process restart reset the scheduler's in-memory lastRunAt map, and markRead calls failed silently under lock contention from a concurrent migration, so sendEmail already fired but the notifications were never marked read. Every subsequent eligible tick re-included the still-unread notifications. Root cause was job-body idempotence, not the restart itself; ADR-016 narrowed cadence policy to separate dispatch throttling from job-level idempotence as a result.

nodes.label: Broken Seed Password Incident (resolved)
nodes.rationale: An earlier seed.ts wrote a literal placeholder string into passwordHash instead of calling hashPassword(SEED_PASSWORD), so no seeded account could log in with any role, on any org. The fixture looked complete in a database browser and the login form's generic invalid-credentials error gave no hint the seed data, not the auth code, was at fault. Fixed by calling hashPassword exactly once per seed run and sharing the resulting hash across accounts, deliberately keeping the salt unpinned so a fixed dev constant is never mistakenly copied into a real deployment.

nodes.label: Single-process, no-external-broker architecture
nodes.rationale: Deliberate architectural choice (ADR-005, narrowed by ADR-016): one scheduler, one in-process queue, no persisted job state beyond process lifetime. Restarting the server resets every job kind's cadence tracking and clears the in-memory queue; this is expected and is the root cause thread running through two of the directory's four postmortems.

nodes.label: In-process typed event bus chosen over external broker
nodes.norm_label: in-process typed event bus chosen over external broker
nodes.rationale: An external broker (Redis Streams) was rejected because it adds an independent failure mode to a corpus meant to run standalone/offline (j.novak). emit()/subscribe() with Promise.allSettled handler isolation was adopted so one failing subscriber cannot block sibling handlers. At-most-once, no-durability delivery was accepted because consumers already re-derive state from source tables rather than trusting event payloads.

nodes.label: Provisional inline webhook delivery decision (later reversed)
nodes.norm_label: provisional inline webhook delivery decision (later reversed)
nodes.rationale: Initial instinct was synchronous inline delivery from the event handler with a bounded timeout, judged simpler and avoiding a second async hop. k.ferreira's prototype later demonstrated a slow/hanging receiver would stall the triggering request; this was reversed by ADR-018, discussed retrospectively in notes-2026-07-13-webhook-secret-rotation.md.

nodes.label: Keyset pagination replaces offset pagination (first wave)
nodes.norm_label: keyset pagination replaces offset pagination (first wave)

Keyset pagination (cursor from sort column + id tiebreaker) avoids both at the cost of no direct 'jump to page N'. Rolled out first for issue, project, and search listings; notification/activity listings deferred since their query pattern already approximates keyset.

nodes.label: Cursor treated as opaque token by every caller
nodes.norm_label: cursor treated as opaque token by every caller

Test strategy asserts cursor stability under concurrent mutation rather than numeric page assertions.

nodes.label: Token-bucket rate limiter table shipped as drafted
nodes.norm_label: token-bucket rate limiter table shipped as drafted
nodes.rationale: member:invite 20/2, comment:create 60/20, issue:create 60/20, search:query 120/60, auth:password-reset 5/1, webhook:deliver 100/50, default 30/10. Cost-weighted limiting for expensive advanced_search field-syntax queries was explicitly deferred (flat per-request limiting shipped first). auth:password-reset is charged per identity, not per organization, since it guards against credential-stuffing independent of plan.

nodes.label: Bucket capacity scaling capped at 100x base
nodes.norm_label: bucket capacity scaling capped at 100x base
nodes.rationale: Capacity scales with apiRequestsPerHour / 100, but capped at 100x rather than letting an enterprise org's raw 1000x multiplier through, because unbounded scaling would let one org's burst overwhelm shared downstream systems the limiter is meant to protect. A single uniform cap (not per-bucket) was chosen for simplicity.

nodes.label: Cadence reframed as dispatch throttle, not correctness guarantee
nodes.norm_label: cadence reframed as dispatch throttle, not correctness guarantee
nodes.rationale: Post-incident review of the digest storm concluded that treating CADENCE_MINUTES as a correctness promise was a category error in ADR-005's original 'hourly by default' framing. j.novak argued durable scheduler state would not have fixed the actual repeat-send mechanism, so the group rejected durable lastRunAt and instead required every job body to tolerate more-frequent-than-cadence execution. This narrows ADR-005 and is formalized as ADR-016.

nodes.label: digest-email markRead retry-on-next-tick fix
nodes.rationale: The digest job's markRead failure path moves from best-effort logging to retrying on the next eligible tick. Per-recipient locking was considered and rejected (d.okafor): queue.ts drain() processes jobs sequentially in one event loop, so overlapping runs are sequential ticks, not true concurrency, making locking unnecessary.

nodes.rationale: s.duarte proposed full removal since it has been on, not plan-gated, for every org since launch. t.abara flagged that integration tests use command_palette's flag context to exercise the 'always on, not overridable' evaluation strategy path in feature-flags.ts, so the wrapper stays in code even though it is no longer meaningful product signal.

nodes.label: Quarterly graduate/remove/keep-gating flag review policy
nodes.rationale: Adopted because ai_issue_summary's 25% rollout had sat unreviewed for months with nobody clearly on the hook. Every flag gets an explicit decision each quarter; a flag unchanged across two consecutive reviews must get a decision at the third. Every new flag must be assigned an explicit owner in the introducing PR.

nodes.label: Rate-limit-before-flag-check ordering is deliberate
nodes.rationale: DES-155 establishes rate limiting runs before the advanced_search flag check specifically so a throttled caller's 429 never leaks whether their plan includes advanced search — checking the flag first would be a minor information disclosure. Confirmed correct despite looking backwards at first glance in a recent code review.

nodes.label: Silent syntax narrowing for advanced_search-gated queries
nodes.norm_label: silent syntax narrowing for advanced_search-gated queries
nodes.rationale: search() in search-service.ts narrows which query features are honored rather than rejecting the whole query when advanced_search is unavailable, to avoid a harsher all-or-nothing failure. A real customer escalation showed this reads as 'broken' rather than 'gated'; the group kept the narrowing but tracked a design proposal to add a response-level 'syntax not honored' signal rather than fixing it same-day.

nodes.label: ADR-018's reversal of ADR-005's inline webhook delivery assumption
nodes.norm_label: adr-018's reversal of adr-005's inline webhook delivery assumption
nodes.rationale: The original event-bus-vs-queue meeting assumed inline synchronous delivery with a bounded timeout would suffice. k.ferreira's prototype demonstrated a slow/hanging receiver would stall the triggering request path, and ADR-018 reversed this in favor of queued delivery with capped exponential backoff (DES-064, shipped today). This meeting is the first time the prototype-driven reason for the reversal was captured in the ops decision log rather than only in the ADR's Context section.

nodes.label: Webhook secret rotation explicitly deferred
nodes.rationale: A customer's security team wants secret rotation without delete-and-recreate (which loses delivery history, DES-214). Two designs considered: in-place (a) vs grace-period dual-secret (b, requires signPayload to accept either secret, touching DES-160's 'pure HMAC wrapper' characterization). In-place alone would create a silent-failure window worse than the current delete-and-recreate workaround, so both were deferred pending stronger demand; DES-159's 'minted once, never regenerated' framing is reaffirmed as a deliberate, reasoned decision, not an oversight.

nodes.label: Build/Typecheck Blind Spot Pattern
nodes.rationale: Three of the last four incidents (digest storm, webhook backlog, board crash) share a gap between what the build/typecheck toolchain can verify and what only shows up at runtime under load or a real render, unlike the cross-tenant leak which was a pure logic/discipline failure. Proposed as a standing design-review criterion: ask whether a build/type failure would catch a regression, and flag it explicitly if correctness instead depends entirely on a remembered convention.

nodes.label: search-reindex Scheduled No-op Gap
nodes.rationale: runSearchReindexJob requires an explicit orgId argument, but the scheduler's tick() enqueues search-reindex with an empty payload, so the scheduled cadence entry is a no-op by construction. The only way the job actually runs is a manual enqueue with an explicit orgId. Documented as a known scaffolding gap, not something to fix mid-incident.

nodes.label: auth-service.ts Event Map Gap
nodes.rationale: auth-service.ts needs to call emit but cannot, because TaskflowEventMap has no login/logout/registration event keys. Judged a genuine design gap, not a layering violation; extending the event map was logged as future work rather than resolved in this meeting, since it would touch every session-related code path.

nodes.label: Issue Detail Page Layering Debt
nodes.rationale: The issue detail page bypasses the existing getIssue service function for no remembered reason; unlike the profile exception this predates a later service-layer addition and was reclassified as real debt scheduled for remediation, not a deliberate permanent choice.

nodes.label: Profile Layering Exception (Permanent)
nodes.rationale: update-profile.ts and the profile page call repositories directly because profile data has no meaningful authorization surface beyond self-identity; judged legitimately permanent, not debt.
